retweet.text:
The bioethics circle jerks during the Human Genome Project, which were allocated 5% of the project's funding, were a total waste of time.

They had countless conferences and workshops imagining bad things that could happen like punitive health insurance rates based on genetic risk, none of which actually came to pass. Meanwhile all the real issues that arose from ubiquitous DNA data, like accidentally doxing your criminal relatives with your own 23andMe data, were never imagined.

It's a condemnation of the precautionary principle. Philosophers can make up all sorts of hypothetical scenarios in a vacuum but it's nothing like actually trying things and seeing all the weird second and third-order consequences that emerge and *then* dealing with the unwelcome ones.

retweet.text:
AgentMail just shipped AgentID, and it's a small feature pointed at a problem that's already out of control.

The idea: an agent gets its own OpenID Connect identity, backed by a verified email and a signing key stored locally. No SDK, just two config values, and it slots straight into Clerk, Supabase, Auth0, and Better Auth. The demo shows an agent signing into Firecrawl and Turso with its own credential instead of a copy of yours.

Here's why that matters right now. GitGuardian's 2026 report found 29 million leaked secrets last year, and flagged AI agent credentials specifically as a category that's spiraling, because the easiest way to give an agent access to anything is still to hand it your API key and hope.

The bigger players agree this is the next infrastructure layer, not a nice to have. Okta launched a Universal Agent Identity Provider this year, in early access, plus a Cross App Access protocol built for agent to app handoffs. Auth0 shipped its own agent identity layer in May. WorkOS added agent registration as a credential type distinct from human users. Twilio went further and acquired Stytch this year specifically for its agent identity and consent tooling, which is about as clear a signal as an acquisition gets.

I keep thinking about how OAuth itself only existed because password sharing between apps became unworkable around 2007. Same shape of problem, new class of actor. We handed agents write access to our inboxes, our databases, our deploy pipelines, and gave almost no thought to how they prove who they are or how you revoke them.

AgentMail is a small startup solving a sliver of this, agent sign in specifically. But the fact that Okta, Auth0, WorkOS, and Twilio are all building some version of the same primitive in the same year tells me identity is about to become as core to agent infra as memory and tool calling already are.

https://t.co/ERG4MMUAze

quote.text:
Money is really a means to an end. And that end is more privacy, convenience, and quietness, and less daily friction in accomplishing things that bring value.

Most people put up with shit because they can't afford to move beyond it. They're stuck in a noisy neighbourhood, with friends who have negative energy, and in extractive employment. As time goes on, their life force gets sapped dry, and they become numb.

What are the lessons here?
1. Get rich and stay away from most people.
2. Be a "high-energy" person.
3. High energy consumption correlates with high GDP. Accomplished individuals also tend to consume a lot of energy (electricity, gas, money, food).
4. If you can't afford a home gym, go to the gym in the early morning when there are no OF girls, annoying and nosy trainers, and nobody fighting you for squat racks/bench press stations/dumbbell benches.

text:
I think every time AI can do something equally good or better than humans it stops being valuable or special

Marketing videos used to take lots of work of editing and motion graphics and a big budget 

Now with Opus 5.5 etc it costs $0 to make one as good or better

That means ANYONE can make a marketing video now, so the timeline gets flooded with these videos (as you see happening now) and people stop caring about them, stop watching them and they stop grabbing attention

The response then to still grab attention is be different and that probably means IRL marketing videos that are original and unique and maybe personal

It's the grim reaper meme where AI keeps commoditizing another media format and bringing the cost down to close to $0

It already did so for graphic design (2023), last year with Nano Banana for photography (2025), this year with Seedance 2.5 it did it for video (2026) and this and next year motion graphics

quote.text:
I've now fully integrated my new site Hotelist into Hoodmaps

So now it lets you tap [ 🏨 Hotels ] and you see all available hotels in the area

You can hover over them or tap them and it'll show the same hover tooltip you see on Hotelist, and then when you tap again it opens the hotel

Nice to find a good area in a city and then book a place there

This was a recommendation by AI to try and monetize Hoodmaps, it gets almost 171,000 vistors per month but never made money in almost a decade, so I asked AI

It makes sense cause hotels are something aligned with when you're trying to find the best area in a city and it makes money!

It only shows when you click [ 🏨 Hotels ] though, so not annoying

quote.text:
I just vibe-coded a B2B SaaS instead of buying it, because the salesperson insisted on a meeting before sending me the price.

Have seen @levelsio write about this and now I experienced it myself.

A salesperson reached out to me on LinkedIn about a platform that uses Apple + Google Wallet to boost webinar show-up rates.

Super smart. We have 20,000 webinar attendees a year at Obsidian, so I wanted to buy it.

I asked for the price. The answer: the fastest way to get one was to book a meeting.

I replied "I don't do calls" and asked them to just send the price so I could buy.

They totally understood, but I still needed a meeting.

So I asked AI to build it into Obsidian's own marketing system (also made by AI and replaced our 4k EUR monthly monday dot com subscription).

About an hour later, I had a working prototype in Google Wallet. 

Apple Wallet is ready too, just waiting on 1–3 days of verification.

Price of their software: no idea, but I would have bought it for $100 monthly immediately if I could.

Price of ours: 1 hour with AI while watching Toy Story 5 with the kids, plus $99 a year for an Apple Developer account. Google was free.

Always envied people who sell b2b saas, but not right now.
